lines: ### The Opening

[q1:1]In the Name of God—the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful. [q1:2]All praise is for God—Lord of all worlds[^1], [q1:3]the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful, [q1:4]Master of the Day of Judgment. [q1:5]You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. [q1:6]Guide us along the Straight Path, [q1:7]the Path of those You have blessed—not those You are displeased with, or those who are astray.[^2][^3][^4]

[v]God did choose Adam and Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Amran above all people:[^5] [v]Offspring, one of the other; and God heareth and knoweth all things. [v]Behold! a woman of the family of Amran was with child and said, O my Lord! I do dedicate unto Thee what is in my womb for Thy special service, so accept it from me. For Thou hearest and knowest all things.[^6] [v]So when she brought it forth, she said, My Lord! surely I have brought it forth a female. (This she said because only a male child could be dedicated to the temple service under the law of Moses, but God knew best what He had willed.) And the male is not like the female. I name the child Mary and commend her and her offspring into Thy protection from the accursed devil.[^7]

[v]And the Lord accepted her with graciousness; He made her grow in purity and beauty and gave her into the charge of Zacharias.[^8] [v]Now Zacharias was a priest who used to burn incense in the temple and exhort people to pray and to glorify God;[^9] his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth:[^10] [v]And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. [v]And they had no child because Elisabeth was barren and they both were now well stricken in years.[^11]

[v]And everytime Zacharias entered the sanctuary to see Mary, he found her supplied with sustenance. He said, O Mary! Whence comes this to thee? She said, From God, for God provides sustenance to whom He pleases without measure.[^12] [v]And as he watched and listened to Mary in the sanctuary, Zacharias prayed in a whisper, O Lord! surely my bones are weakened and my head flares with hoariness, and my Lord! I have never been unblest in my prayer to Thee. [v]Now I fear what my relatives will do after me, and my wife is barren, so grant me from Thyself an heir.

[v]Who receives my heritage and the heritage of the children of Jacob, and make him, O my Lord, one in whom thou art well pleased.[^13][^14] [v]And it came to pass that Zacharias was burning incense in the temple and a multitude of the people were praying without. [v]And there appeared to him angels, and they said, God gives thee the good news of a son, whose name shall be John, verifying a word from God.[^15] [v]He will be honourable and chaste and a prophet and of the goodly company of the righteous. And God has not made any one true to the name John before him.

[v]Zacharias said, O’ my Lord! how shall I have a son, when my wife is barren and I have grown quite decrepit from age? [v]The angels said, So it will be: thy Lord saith, It is easy for Me. I did indeed create thee before when thou hadst been nothing. [v]Zacharias said, O my Lord! Give me a sign. He answered, Thy sign shall be that thou shalt speak to no man for three days and three nights except by signs, although thou art not dumb. [v]Then Zacharias came out from the sanctuary, and he told people by signs to glorify God in the morning and in the evening.[^16]

[v]And God cured the barrenness of Elisabeth, and she bore John that God may annoint him to be the priest of the house of Aaron[^17] whom He promised to Israel aforetime. [v]So peace on John, the day that he was born, and the day that he will die and the day that he will be raised to life again!

[v]And as for Mary, it came to pass that she withdrew from her people to a place in the east. [v]She placed a screen to screen herself from them; then God sent His angel, and he appeared before her as a man in all respects. [v]She said, I seek refuge from thee to the Most Gracious: come not near me if thou dost fear God. [v]He said, Nay, I am but a messenger of God to thee.[^18] [v]O Mary! God hath chosen thee and purified thee—chosen thee above the women of all nations. [v]O Mary! worship thy Lord devoutly, prostrate thyself, and bow in prayer with those who bow down.

[v]O Mary! God giveth thee the good news of a word from Him; his name will be Jesus the Messiah.[^19] He will be held in honour in this world and the world to come and will be of the company of those nearest to God.[^20][^21][^22] [v]He shall speak to the people in infancy and in manhood, and he shall be of the company of the righteous[^23] [v]He shall be an example to the children of Israel and a knowledge for the hour.[^24] [v]Mary said, O my Lord! How shall I have a son when no man hath touched me and I am not unchaste?

[v]He said, Even so it shall be: God createth what He willeth; for when He decides upon a plan, He saith to it, “Be”! and it is.[^25] [v]Because Jesus was made with God’s creative word “Be,” he was called a word from God. [v]So she conceived him, and she retired with him to a remote place.[^26] [v]And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree, and she cried, Ah! would that I had died before this! Would that I had been a thing forgotten and out of sight! [v]But a voice cried to her from beneath the palm tree, Grieve not, for thy Lord hath provided a rivulet beneath thee;[^27] [v]And shake towards thyself the trunk of the tree: it will let fall fresh ripe dates upon thee.

[v]So eat and drink and cool thine eyes. If thou dost see any man, say, I have vowed a fast to the Most Gracious, and this day I enter into no talk with any human being.[^28] [v]Then she came to her people carrying the babe in her arms. They said, O Mary! Truly an amazing thing thou hast brought. [v]O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a man of evil, nor thy mother a woman unchaste![^29] [v]But she pointed to the babe. They said, How can we talk to an infant in the cradle.[^30] [v]But the child spoke up and said, I am indeed a servant of God. He hath appointed me as a sign for men and a mercy from Him. This was a matter decreed.

[v]He will give me the Book and make me His messenger to the children of Israel. [v]That I may verify the Torah and make lawful for Israel part of what was forbidden to them. [v]That I may teach to them wisdom and make clear to them some of the things, in which they disputed.[^31]

[v]That I may bring to the world the good news of a messenger who will come after me as light and mercy to all the nations; his name shall be called Admirable.[^32] [v]And he will be of the family of Abraham, as God promised to him saying, In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed[^33] [v]And he will be from Kedar, a tribe of the children of Ishmael, the son of Abraham. [v]As Esias prophesied, saying, Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voices in rejoicing, the villages that Kedar doth inhabit[^34] [v]And he shall come from Mount Paran, as Moses spoke of him, saying, God came from Mount Paran with ten thousand saints[^35] [v]And when he is come, he will guide the nations into all truth, for he shall not speak of himself but whatsoever he hears that shalt he speak and coming things he will announce to you.[^36]

[v]He shall not fail nor be discouraged till he have set justice in the earth, and the isles shall wait for his law.[^37] [v]For God did choose the family of Abraham and the family of Amran and Adam and Noah over the people of all nations. [v]And God heareth and knoweth all things.[^38] [v]When Mary’s people heard this, they marveled at it. They said one to another, What do we about this marvelous babe? People will not believe what we have heard and seen. [v]One of them, Joseph[^39] of Bethlehem, said, I wed her and take her and the babe to Bethlehem, and then we return to Nazareth after a period.[^40] And so it was done.

[v]And before God the creation of Jesus is like the creation of Adam. He made him from dust and then said to him, “Be,” and he was.[^41] [v]This is the true account; and there is no God besides God, the exalted in power, the wise[^42] [v]He is self-sustaining, and He begetteth not, nor is He begotten. [v]And there is none like unto Him.[^43]

[v]And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus, which is how he was named by the angel of God before he was conceived in the womb. [v]And when the days of Mary’s purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord; [v]As it is written, Every male that openeth a womb shall be called holy to the Lord. [v]And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is written in the law, A pair of turtle-doves, or two young pigeons.

[v]And, behold, there was a just and devout man in Jerusalem, Simeon by name. [v]When he saw the child, he took him from his parents in his arms and blessed God and said, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rise of many in Israel and for a sign for the people. [v]He shall prepare the way for a light to lighten the nations.[^44] [v]And after some time, Joseph and Mary returned with the boy Jesus to Nazareth. [v]And there he grew and waxed strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was with him.[^45]

[v]And none but a few knew that he was not Joseph’s son but was created by God without a father, even as Adam was created without father or mother[^46] [v]Now Joseph and Mary went to Jerusalem every year of the Passover. [v]And when Jesus was twelve or thirteen years old, they went up to Jerusalem with him, to make him a son of the law, after the custom of the Jews.[^47] [v]This meant that Jesus was now responsible for the commandments of the law. [v]And when the ceremony was completed, and the days were fulfilled,[^48] the caravan missed Jesus, and he was left behind in Jerusalem, but Joseph and his mother knew not of it.

[v]And they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day’s journey; and they sought him among their kinfolk and acquaintances. [v]And when they found him not, they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him. [v]And it came to pass that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them and asking them questions. [v]And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.[^49] [v]And when he went with Joseph and Mary, his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us: Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.

[v]And he said unto them, Ye knew that I have to be in these matters that are God’s.[^50] [v]And the family returned to their home in Galilee. [v]And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature and in favour with God and men.

chapters.title: John and the Beginning of the Ministry

lines: [v]And John, the son of Zacharias, too, was given wisdom and good judgement even as a youth: [v]He grew up in the wilderness to be tender to all creatures; and he was pure and devout; [v]Kind to his parents; and he was not overbearing or rebellious.[^51] [v]He renounced the pleasures of this world and preferred garments of camel’s hair over soft raiment; and he did eat locusts and wild honey.[^52] [v]And in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, and Herod Antipas was the Tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip the Tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the Tetrarch of Abilene; and when Caiaphas and his father-in-law were the high priests, [v]A word from God came unto John in the wilderness, and he began to preach in the country about the river Jordan, [v]Saying, Repent and reform for the day of the Lord is drawing near.

[v]And he administered the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. [v]Then went out to him whole Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region round about Jordan, [v]To be baptized of him in Jordan and to confess their sins. [v]And baptizing them, he said, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? [v]Bring forth, therefore, fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say that we have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

[v]And now also the axe is laid unto the roots of the trees: every tree, therefore, which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire. [v]And the people asked him, saying, What shall we do then? [v]He answered and saith unto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart one to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise. [v]And there also came tax collectors to be baptized and said unto him, Master, what shall we do? [v]And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed to you.

[v]And soldiers likewise asked him, saying, And what shall we do? [v]And he said unto them, Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely, and be content with your wages.[^53] [v]And as the people were in expectation, all men mused in their hearts of John whether he was the Messiah of Aaron, or the Messiah of Israel, or that Prophet[^54] [v]John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed am annointed to be the priest of the house of Aaron, who was to come in the last days, [v]And from among my disciples whom I have baptized there shall arise the Messiah of Israel.
[v]And as for that prophet, of whom God has been promising through the mouths of all his messengers, he will come after us to be a light for the nations.

[v]And Jesus was about thirty years of age,[^55] and he came from Galilee to Jordan unto John to be baptized of him. [v]And when he was baptized, he went up out of the water, and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Holy Spirit descending like a dove and lighting upon him, [v]And he heard a voice from heaven,[^56] saying, Thou art of the three I have chosen.[^57] [v]Then Jesus knew that this was the hour of his appointment[^58] as a messenger of God to Israel. [v]That he may support and continue John’s work[^59] of reform of Israel and prepare the way for the light which will lighten the nations.

[v]But in his mind the devil started to put doubts about this.[^60] [v]And Jesus, perplexed, retired in the wilderness to be by himself; but the devil followed him. [v]And when Jesus hungered, the devil said, If thou be a chosen of God, command this stone that it be made bread. [v]But Jesus answered unto him, It is written that man shall not live by bread alone but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. [v]Then the devil saith unto him, If thou be a chosen of God, go to Jerusalem, set thyself on the pinnacle of the temple,[^61] and cast thyself down; for it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee to keep thee, [v]And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.

[v]And Jesus, answering, said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not test the Lord thy God. [v]And then the devil showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory and said unto him, All this power and glory I will give thee. [v]If thou, therefore, wilt worship me, all shall be thine. [v]And Jesus answered and said unto him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and Him only shalt thou serve. [v]With the power of these words, the devil went away. [v]And Jesus came to John and told him what happened to him, and John witnessed the truth of the voice from heaven.[^62] And he said unto him, Wait for the word of God.

[v]And Jesus wandered with John in Judea and they went as far as Aenon near Salim.[^63] [v]And John, fearing no one but God, boldly reproved Herod the Tetrarch of Galilee for marrying Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, [v]Saying, it is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife. [v]And for many other things did John reprove Herod, and he also reproved Herodias for adultery. [v]But Herod Antipas added yet this above all his evils, that he put John in prison.[^64] [v]Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee,[^65] and tarried in Nazareth, where he was brought up.[^66]

[v]And on a sabbath day, as his custom was, he went to the synagogue. [v]And the attendant stood up with the Scriptures waiting for someone to come and read a passage and explain it. [v]And that sabbath day it was Jesus who stood up to read. [v]And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esias; and when he opened the book, he found the place where it was written, [v]The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath annointed me to preach the good news unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives.

[v]To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of vengeance of our God. [v]And having read the passage, he closed the book and gave it back to the attendant and sat down; and the eyes of all those that were in the synagogue were fastened on him.[^67] [v]And he stood up again and began to say unto them, This day is this Scripture fulfilled in your ears. [v]When people heard this, they said one to another, Is not this the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary? and his brothers James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas: And are not his sisters here with us?

[v]And they were offended that one among them should speak of himself as a prophet of God. [v]But Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, no prophet is accepted in his own city. [v]But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias,[^68] when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land; [v]But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto a widow of Sarepta, a city of Sidon. [v]And many lepers there were in Israel in the city of Eliseus the prophet, and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.

[v]And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath, [v]And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him into the brow of the hill whereon the city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.[^69] [v]But he escaped them and went his way; and leaving Nazareth he went towards Capernaum,[^70] a city of Galilee. [v]Preaching on the way, Repent, for the day of the Lord is drawing near.[^71]

[v]And there were in Capernaum many disciples of John the Baptist,[^72] and two of them were Andrew and his brother Simon. [v]And they took Jesus to their house,[^73] and there he found that the mother of Simon’s wife was sick of a fever. [v]And Jesus stood over her, took her hand, and prayed to the Lord, [v]And the fever left her and she arose.[^74] [v]And on the sabbath day Jesus went to the synagogue and began to preach to the people there, [v]Saying, O children of Israel, fear the day of the Lord when your father Abraham will be no wise able to save you, [v]Say not therefore within yourself, We have Abraham to our father: for, as John said to you, God is able of stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

[v]Neither is salvation by the law of Moses alone, but by faith in the One True Living God, [v]Who is my Creator and your Creator, my Lord and your Lord; so serve Him and Him alone. This is the way that is straight.[^75] [v]As Jesus was speaking these words, there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out, [v]Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? Art thou come to destroy us? [v]And Jesus said unto the spirit, By the permission of the One True Living God, I command thee to come out of him.

[v]And when the spirit had torn him and cried with a loud voice, it came out of him. [v]And the people there were amazed,[^76] but some were offended because of what he said about Abraham and the Law of Moses, even though he had said nothing against them. [v]But those who admired him took his fame into every place of the country round about. [v]And at even, when the sun was set, people brought unto him all that were diseased and that were possessed with demons. [v]And a multitude gathered together at the door of the house of Andrew and Simon.

[v]And he laid his hands on every one of those that were diseased and those that were possessed with demons, and as many as God willed were healed.[^77] [v]And one morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed. [v]And Simon and Andrew and other people followed after him. [v]And when they had found him, they said unto him, All men seek thee. [v]And he said unto them, Let us go in the next towns, that I may preach there, also; for therefore came I away. [v]And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee and cast out devils.[^78]
[v]And the scribes and the rulers of the synagogue began to be offended by him because of what he preached and because the people admired him for the healings.

[v]And it came to pass that there came a leper, beseeching him, and saying unto him, If thou art willing, thou canst make me clean. [v]And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand and touched him and said unto him, Be thou clean! [v]Then, strongly admonishing him, immediately he sent him away, [v]Saying, See thou say nothing to any man, but go and show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded.[^79] [v]And it came to pass on the second sabbath of the first month, that Jesus and his disciples passed through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked ears of corn and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.

[v]And certain of the Pharisees saw them and said unto them, Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days? [v]And Jesus, answering them, said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungered, and they which were with him, [v]How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar, the high priest, and did take and eat the shew bread, and gave also to them that were with him, which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests? [v]And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for sabbath; therefore a man is lord of the sabbath and not sabbath the lord of man.[^80]

[v]And Jesus began to preach out of the synagogues to the poor and to the publicans and sinners.[^81] [v]And one day he went up a mount, and his disciples were gathered around him and a multitude with them. [v]And he began to preach, Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. [v]Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted. [v]Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth. [v]Blessed are they that do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled. [v]Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

[v]Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God. [v]Blessed are the peace makers: for they shall be called the children of God. [v]Blessed are they that are persecuted for righteousness sake: for great is their reward in heaven.[^82] [v]And many other things did he preach, and when he was finished, the people were astonished at his doctrine. [v]For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.[^83]

[v]And Jesus also preached among the publicans who worked for the Roman rulers to collect tax and custom. [v]And one publican named Levi became his disciple. [v]And Levi made him a great feast in his house, and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them. [v]But the scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners. [v]And Jesus, answering to what they murmured, said unto his disciples, They that are whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.

[v]I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentence[^84] [v]And some of the scribes and Pharisees also said, Why do his disciples eat and dine and not fast often as did John. [v]And Jesus said, Whereunto shall I liken the men of this generation? and unto what are they like? [v]They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We piped unto you and ye did not dance, we mourned and ye did not weep. [v]For John came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and they say, He hath a demon.

[v]And I have come eating and drinking and they say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a wine-bibber, and a friend of publicans and sinners. [v]But wisdom is justified by all her children.[^85] [v]And the disciples of John reported to him of all these things.[^86] [v]And John sent two of his disciples, and said unto him, Art thou he that should come with me?[^87] or look we for another? [v]When the men were come unto him, they said, John hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come with me? or look we for another?

[v]And Jesus answered and said, Blessed is he, if he does not doubt me.[^88] [v]I came not to destroy the sabbath or fasting but only those who make them lords over man.[^89] [v]And I came not to destroy the law or the prophets, but to confirm them.[^90] [v]And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak concerning John, saying, I tell you among those born of women there is none greater than John the Baptist. [v]And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
[v]But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.[^91]

[v]Then came together unto him certain of the Pharisees and the scribes from Jerusalem.[^92] [v]And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with unwashen hands, they found fault. [v]For the Pharisees and many of the Jews held that if food is eaten with unwashen hands, it is defiled. [v]And they asked Jesus, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands? [v]He answered and said unto them; Well hath Esias said of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.

[v]Howbeit in vain do they worship Me, and their fear toward Me is taught by the precept of men.[^93] [v]For ye teach the traditions of men as commandments of God[^94] and lay aside what God commanded. [v]For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die: [v]But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Korban, that is, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free. [v]And ye suffer him no more to do aught for his father or his mother.[^95]

[v]Making the word of God of none effect. [v]And when he had come away from the people and entered into a house, he received the Spirit and testified and said unto his disciples, Verily, verily, I say unto you, No prophet from Israel will be sent to uproot their traditions. [v]For no man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; and no man putteth new wine into old bottles; but new wine must be put into new bottles. [v]For this cause will the Lord raise a prophet from the midst of another nation, and put His word into his mouth, that He may uproot every plant which He hath not planted;[^96] that He may give unto the world a new wine that men of all nations may quench their thirst.

[v]After these things it came to pass that there came to Jesus a Greek woman, Syrophoenician by nation: [v]Her daughter had an unclean spirit, and she besought Jesus that he would cast it out of her. [v]But he answered her not a word; and his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us. [v]But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.[^97] [v]Howbeit I know another man of God, and she can go to him, for he taketh devils out of all kinds of people.

[v]And Jesus continued to travel and preach for the spiritual renewal of Israel; and when he was preaching in Bethsaida, people brought to him a blind man that he may heal him. [v]And he spit on his finger and rubbed the eyes of the blind man, and asked him if he saw ought, [v]And he looked up and said, I see men as trees walking. [v]After that he put his fingers again upon his eyes, and made him look up; and by God’s healing power he was restored and saw every man clearly.[^98] [v]And one day Jesus was traveling and he came to a well.[^99]

[v]And being wearied with his journey, sat on the well; and it was about the sixth hour. [v]Then there cometh a woman to draw water: Jesus saith to her, thou hast six pitchers of water at home, how many more thou needest? [v]The woman was amazed that Jesus knew what she had in her house and saith unto him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. [v]Jesus saith unto her, Today for thy first meal, thou ate butter and honey after a long time, but to what Jacob and the prophets and I call my people is better sustenance than this water and butter and honey.

[v]And it can give thee what the two husbands thou have hadst could not give thee. [v]The woman was therefore amazed all the more that Jesus also knew her past. She saith unto him, Sir, what is it that Jacob and the other prophets and thou call us to and is better than this water and the butter and honey I ate today and the two husbands I have had? [v]Jesus answering unto her saith, Worship ye the One True God who created me and you and who provides us with our daily sustenance, [v]Worship ye Him in spirit and in truth,[^100] and besides Him worship none, for it can neither profit nor harm.

[v]And upon this came some of his disciples (who had gone away to the city to buy meat), and the woman then left, and went her way to the city. ### Do Not Say Trinity

[q4:170]O humanity! The Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe for your own good. But if you disbelieve, then know that to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise. [q4:171]O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes regarding your faith; say nothing about God except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of God and the fulfilment of His Word through Mary and a spirit created by a command from Him[^151]. So believe in God and His messengers and do not say, “Trinity.” Stop!—for your own good. God is only One God. Glory be to Him! He is far above having a son! To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And God is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs. [q4:172]The Messiah would never be too proud to be a servant of God, nor would the angels nearest to God. Those who are too proud and arrogant to worship Him will be brought before Him all together. [q4:173]As for those who believe and do good, He will reward them in full and increase them out of His grace. But those who are too proud and arrogant, He will subject them to a painful punishment. And besides God they will find no protector or helper.[^152]
### One God, Not Three

The Messiah himself said, “O Children of Israel! Worship God—my Lord and your Lord.” Whoever associates others with God in worship will surely be forbidden Paradise by God. Their home will be the Fire. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers. [q5:72][q5:73]Those who say, “God is one in a Trinity,” have certainly fallen into disbelief. There is only One God. If they do not stop saying this, those who disbelieve among them will be afflicted with a painful punishment. [q5:74]Will they not turn to God in repentance and seek His forgiveness? And God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger. Many messengers had come and gone before him. His mother was a woman of truth. They both ate food[^153]. See how We make the signs clear to them, yet see how they are deluded from the truth! Say, O Prophet, “How can you worship besides God those who can neither harm nor benefit you? And God alone is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.” Say, “O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes in your faith beyond the truth, nor follow the vain desires of those who went astray before you. They misled many and strayed from the Right Way.”[^154]

[v]And Jesus entered into Jerusalem, and thus was fulfilled one part of the prophecy of Esias, in which it is written, He saw two riders, one of them was a rider upon an ass, and the other a rider upon a camel[^161] [v]And about the first rider, it is written, Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy king cometh, sitting upon a colt the foal of an ass.[^162] [v]And when he was come into Jerusalem, people asked each other, saying, Who is this? [v]And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.[^163]

[v]And Jesus went into the temple: and when he had looked round about upon all things, and now the eventide was come, he went out unto Bethany with the twelve.[^164] [v]And he said unto them, I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled? [v]And I have a baptism to be baptized with and how am I pressed until it is accomplished. [v]Think not that I am come to send peace, but a sword. [v]For from henceforth there shall be five in a household divided, three against two, and two against three. [v]The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother, and the brothers and sisters against the brothers and sisters.[^165]

[v]And on the morrow, they returned to Jerusalem: and Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money changers, and the seats of them that sold doves. [v]And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple. [v]And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer,[^166] but ye have made it a den of thieves. [v]And the scribes and chief priests heard about it, but could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.[^167]

[v]The next day Jesus cometh again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, there came to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders, [v]And say unto him, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority to do these things? [v]And Jesus answered and said unto them, I will also ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things. [v]The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? Answer me. [v]And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did ye not believe him?

[v]But if we shall say, Of men; they feared the people: for all men counted John, that he was a prophet indeed. [v]And they answered and said unto Jesus, We cannot tell. And Jesus answering saith unto them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things[^168] [v]After that they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.[^169] [v]And when they were come, they say unto him, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

[v]Shall we give, or shall we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said unto them, Why tempt ye me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it. [v]And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Caesar’s. [v]And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s. [v]And they could not take hold of his words before the people, but they held their peace. [v]Then come unto him certain of the Sadducees, which say there is no resurrection and they asked him, saying, [v]Teacher, Moses wrote unto us, If a man’s brother die, and leave his wife behind him, and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

[v]Now there were seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed. [v]And the second took her, and died, neither left he any seed: and the third likewise. [v]And the seven had her, and left no seed: last of all the woman died also. [v]In the resurrection therefore, when they shall rise, whose wife shall she be of them? For the seven had her to wife. [v]And Jesus answering said unto them, Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God? [v]For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage.

[v]And as touching the dead, that they rise from the dead: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? [v]For He is not the God of the dead, but of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.[^170] [v]And one of the scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, asked him, Which is the first commandment of all? [v]And Jesus answered and said, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord:

[v]And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. [v]And the second is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these. [v]And the scribe said unto him, Well, Teacher, thou hast said the truth: for there is one God; and there is none other but he: [v]And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is more than all the burnt offerings and sacrifices.
[v]And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.[^171]

[v]Then spoke Jesus to his disciples, Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: [v]All therefore that they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not. [v]All their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments, [v]And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, [v]And greetings in the market places, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.[^172] [v]And after two days was the feast of the passover, and of unleavened bread; and the chief priests, and the scribes sought how they might take him by craft.

[v]But they said, Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar of the people;[^173] even though many of the people would not fight for Jesus. [v]And Jesus knowing that the chief priests and the scribes sought now to take him by force, he hid himself with his disciples.[^174] [v]Thus ended the public ministry of this messenger of God to Israel. He came to his people with a sign from their Lord in that he would make for them the figure of a bird out of clay, and would breath into it and it would become a bird by God’s leave:

[v]And he would heal those born blind, and the lepers, and would quicken the dead by God’s leave: [v]And he would declare unto them what they ate, and what they stored in their houses. [v]Surely in this there was sign for them if they did have any faith. [v]But they received him not, save a few. [v]And the unbelievers plotted and God too planned, and God is the best of planners[^175] [v]He made Jesus’ entry into Jerusalem and the unbelievers plots a means of their own punishment and a means for the coming of the Saviour of the nations.[^176]

[v]And this is the parable concerning the children of Israel and the prophets sent to them. [v]A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the wine fat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country. [v]And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from them of the fruit of the vineyard. [v]And they caught him, and beat him, and sent him away empty. [v]And again he sent unto them another servant; and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.

[v]And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some. [v]The lord of the vineyard therefore came and destroyed the husbandmen, and gave the vineyard unto others. [v]So likewise God will take away the kingdom of heaven from the children of Israel because of the way they treated John and Jesus and other prophets, and He will give it to the children of Ishmael and Kedar: [v]As the Scriptures say, The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner. [v]This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes.[^177]

[v]Thus did God make the coming of Jesus a preparation for the Saviour of the nations, and Jesus did indeed announce his coming. [v]As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee. [v]And the night Jesus hid himself from the world, he had a vision and he saw a fig tree, very old and without much fruit. [v]And he saw people coming to it, and seeking of its fruit that they might satisfy their hunger and thirst, but they find nothing but leaves. [v]And Jesus curseth the fig tree and it withered from the roots.
[v]Then there came another planter from afar and he planted a tree that it might give fruit unto the end of time. [v]And people of all kinds came to it and ate of its fruit.[^178]
### Distorting the Scripture

[q3:78]There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues to make you think this distortion is from the Book—but it is not what the Book says. They say, “It is from God”—but it is not from God. And so they attribute lies to God knowingly.[^179]
### Prophets Never Claim Divinity

[q3:79]It is not appropriate for someone who God has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people, “Worship me instead of God.” Rather, he would say, “Be devoted to the worship of your Lord alone”—in accordance with what these prophets read in the Scripture and what they taught. [q3:80]And he would never ask you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted?[^180]
### Disputes over Jesus

[q3:61]Now, whoever disputes with you O Prophet concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you, say, “Come! Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves—then let us sincerely invoke God’s curse upon the liars.” [q3:63]If they turn away, then surely God has perfect knowledge of the corruptors. [q3:64]Say, O Prophet, “O People of the Book! Let us come to common terms: that we will worship none but God, associate none with Him, nor take one another as lords instead of God.” But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we have submitted to God alone.”[^181]

[v]And the next day Jesus said to his disciples, He that hath a purse, let him take it, and he that hath no sword, let him sell his garment, and buy one. [v]For I say unto you, that this that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors. [v]And they brought two swords and showed these to Jesus, and he said, By God’s leave, it is enough for the faithless.[^182] [v]Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went unto the chief priests, to betray him unto them. [v]And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.

[v]And the first day of unleavened bread, when they killed the passover, his disciples said unto him, Where wilt thou we go and prepare that thou mayest eat the passover? [v]And he sendeth forth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go ye into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The Teacher saith, Where will I keep the passover with my disciples? [v]And he will take you to a large upper room, and there make ready for us. [v]And his disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.[^183]

[v]And when they had sung an hymn, and the supper was ended,[^184] Jesus began to teach them, and to tell them all things that must come to pass after him, [v]Saying, I came to reform the traditions of the elders, and to clean the house of prayer, but my people seek to kill me. [v]Verily I say unto you, the temple is no more a house of God, but a den of thieves, and a symbol of the dead past; [v]And there shall come a time, when this structure of stones shall be thrown down, and destroyed with utter destruction.[^185] [v]And God will smite the children of Israel, because that they rejected His messengers, and will scatter them like unto sheep without a shepherd.

[v]And then there shall arise the Man[^186] of perfection with great power and glory; and he will build a new house of prayer, that men may worship the One True Living God in spirit and in truth. [v]And he will be a staff to the righteous, on which they will support themselves and not fall, and he will be the light of the nations, and the hope of those who are troubled in heart. [v]All who dwell on earth will fall down, and bow the knee after him, and bless and laud and celebrate the Lord. [v]And for this cause has he been chosen before the creation of the world; and before the sun and the signs were created, before the stars of heaven were made, his name was named before the Lord.[^187]

[v]Peter therefore asked Jesus, Teacher, tell us what is that blessed name. [v]And Jesus answering said, His name shall be Admirable Counsellor, as it is prophesied by Esias: [v]For us a child is given, for us a son is born: and the dominion shall be upon his shoulder and his name shall be called Admirable Counsellor, Angel of Mighty Counsel.[^188] [v]And when he is come, the kings of the earth, and the strong who possess the power, will be of downcast countenance and the word of his mouth shall slay them; for God will put His own words in his mouth, as He promised to Moses.

[v]Saying, I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and I will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him. And it shall come to pass that whosoever will not hearken unto My words which he shall speak in My name, I will require a reckoning of him.[^189] [v]And all the people of the world will hearken unto his words, save those who follow the way of the Antichrist. [v]For the Antichrist covers me and hides the truth from them. [v]Howbeit when he will be let loose, God will destroy him, and will reveal me again, and the stumbling-block will be removed.
[v]Then will all the nations of the world follow the Counsellor, and bless and laud and worship the One True Living God.

[v]Then the disciples asked Jesus, Teacher, when will the end be? [v]And Jesus answering said unto them, Of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not even the angels in heaven, but only the Lord.[^190] [v]For the prophets know nothing of the future which they are not taught, and they see nothing which they are not shown. [v]Watch therefore: for ye know not when the day of our Lord cometh. [v]For as the days of Noah were, so shall also the day of our Lord be. [v]For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, [v]And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away so shall the coming of the day of our Lord be.[^191]

[v]And it is also known only to God how much longer shall I abide with you. [v]I therefore bid you that ye keep my words, and follow the Law according to what I have taught you. [v]That ye worship the One True Living God in spirit and in truth, and that ye love one another. [v]It is expedient for you that I go away, for if I go not away the Counsellor[^192] will not come. [v]But if I go away, God will send him, that he may teach all the nations, [v]And abide with them unto the end of the age. [v]I have yet many things to tell you, but ye cannot bear them now.

[v]Howbeit when the Counsellor, the Spirit of truth, is come he will guide you into all truth and teach you all things, for he shall not speak of himself but what things he shall hear that shall he speak; and he will declare things that are to come. [v]He shall glorify me, because he will receive from the same Spirit, of which I have received[^193] [v]And after these sayings Jesus solemnly took the covenant of the prophets from his followers. [v]Saying, God hath given you wisdom and a book. Then cometh to you the Counsellor confirming what is with you, do ye believe and render him help? Do ye agree and take this God’s covenant as binding on you?
[v]They said, We do. And Jesus said, Then bear witness, and God is with you among the witnesses.[^194]
### A Clear Book from God

[q5:15]O People of the Book! Now Our Messenger (Muhammad) has come to you, revealing much of what you have hidden of the Scriptures and disregarding much. There certainly has come to you from God a light and a clear Book [q5:16]through which God guides those who seek His pleasure to the ways of peace, brings them out of darkness and into light by His Will, and guides them to the Straight Path.[^195]
### Jesus Prophesied the Coming of Muhammad

[q61:6]And remember when Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O children of Israel! I am truly God’s messenger to you, confirming the Torah which came before me, and giving good news of a messenger after me whose name will be Aḥmad[^196].” Yet when the Prophet came to them with clear proofs, they said, “This is pure magic.” [q61:7]Who does more wrong than the one who fabricates lies about God when invited to submit[^197] to Him? For God does not guide the wrongdoing people.[^198]

[v]Then Jesus got up, and he and his disciples went out to the mount of Olives, but Judas Iscariot did not go with them. Couldest not thou watch one hour? [v]And again he went away, and prayed that the plots of the faithless against his life be defeated. [v]And when he returned, he found them asleep again (for their eyes were heavy) neither wist they what to answer him.

[v]Then he heard some men, and he saith unto his disciples, Arise, let us go hence; behold, he that betrayeth me hath drawn near. [v]But while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a number of men with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders. [v]And as soon as they were come, Judas goeth straightway to him, and saith, Teacher, and then kissed him fervently. [v]And by this they knew the man they had come to take, and they laid their hands on Jesus, and took him. [v]And one of them that stood by (some say it was Peter) drew a sword, but when he saw the multitude of men with swords and staves, he and the other disciples fled.[^202]

[v]And they led Jesus away to the high priest. [v]And Simon Peter went to the house of a disciple who was known unto the high priest, and taking him goes to the palace of the high priest.[^203] [v]And while Peter stood at the door without, the other disciple went into the palace, and saw Jesus before the high priest and the elders and the scribes and chief priests. [v]Then he went out, and spoke unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter. [v]And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter came and stood with them, and warmed himself.

[v]Then saith the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Art thou of this man’s disciples.[^204] He saith, I am not. [v]But the maid began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them. [v]And he denied it again. But they that stood by said unto him, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilean, and thy speech agreeth thereto. ### Conspiracy Against Jesus

[q3:55]Remember when God said, “O Jesus! I will take you[^205] and raise you up to Myself. I will deliver you from those who disbelieve, and elevate your followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment. Then to Me you will all return, and I will settle all your disputes. [q3:56]As for those who disbelieve, I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers. [q3:57]And as for those who believe and do good, they will be rewarded in full. And God does not like the wrongdoers.” [q3:58]We recite all this to you O Prophet as one of the signs[^206] and as a wise reminder.[^207]

[v]And the chief priests and all the council sought evidence against Jesus to put him to death; and found none. [v]For many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together. [v]And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? What is it which these witness against thee? [v]But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, Art thou the Messiah? [v]And Jesus said, Thou sayest it. Nevertheless, the One Living God has annointed me to be His messenger to the children of Israel. If they would have received me, He would have given to them a kingdom like He gave unto David.

[v]But ye had indeed rejected faith: so pursue your plans, and God will execute His plan; and He is the best of planners. [v]Then some of those in the council rose up, and said, What need we any further evidence? [v]Ye have heard that he setteth himself up as a King and the Messiah, and he did earlier enter into Jerusalem on the back of a colt, pretending to be the King of the Jews. [v]Deliver him therefore to Pilate that he may crucify him for setting himself up as a King besides Caesar.[^208] [v]And in the morning they brought him before Pontius Pilate, the governor, and said, We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is the Messiah, a king.

[v]And Pilate asked him, Knowest thou what thy people witness against thee? Art thou the King of the Jews.[^209] [v]Jesus answered, My kingdom is not like thy kingdom: if my kingdom was like thine, then would I have soldiers to fight that I should not be delivered to thee by my people: but my kingdom is not like thine. [v]Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king of thy people then? [v]And Jesus answering said unto him, How wouldst thou call a messenger to his people from the King of kings? [v]Then the Jews who brought Jesus to Pilate said unto him, He hath said it; and thou knowest that whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.

[v]Then Pilate brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgement seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.[^210] [v]Now at that feast Pilate was wont to release unto the people one prisoner, whomsoever they desired;[^212] and they asked for Barabbas,[^213] a notable prisoner[^214] who had made an insurrection, and Pilate released Barabbas unto them. [v]And he pronounced sentence upon Jesus, that he should go upon the cross, and delivered him to be flogged.[^211]

[v]And when they led him away to crucify him, God took Jesus up unto Himself; and they killed him not, nor crucified him, but it was made to appear so unto them.[^215] [v]For the likeness of Jesus was cast upon another, and they crucified him whom they took for Jesus; and the soldiers, and the people that stood by, and the women that watched afar off, all supposed that it was he.[^216] [v]And the chief priests boasted, saying, We have killed the Messiah, Jesus the son of Mary, the messenger of God; but they killed him not: and they that argue about it unto this day are in doubt about it, and have no knowledge of it, but follow conjecture.[^219] [v]Thus the unbelievers plotted, and God planned, and God is the best of planners: He purified Jesus from those who disbelieved, and set those who follow him above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection.[^220]
### Jesus Was Neither Killed nor Crucified

[q4:157]And for boasting, “We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of God.” But they neither killed nor crucified him—it was only made to appear so.[^217] Even those who argue for this crucifixion are in doubt. They have no knowledge whatsoever—only making assumptions. They certainly did not kill him. [q4:158]Rather, God raised him up to Himself. And God is Almighty, All-Wise.[^218]

[v]And Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor who also waited for the kingdom of God, went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of him that was crucified, supposing it to be the body of Jesus.[^221] [v]And he took it down, and wrapped it in fine linen, and laid it in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre. [v]And very early in the morning of the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and other women came unto the sepulchre with sweet spices, that they might anoint the body. [v]And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre, and the body was not there; and they were greatly affrighted, and fled, and said nothing to any man.[^222]

[v]And there went around divers sayings among the people concerning Jesus. Some said, He was crucified and buried, and is risen from the dead; and some said, He was crucified, and they have taken away his body; and some said, He was not crucified at all, but another in his likeness, and God hath taken him up unto Himself.[^223] [v]And the disciples that had fled were scattered, every man to his own; and some of them said that they had seen him: but they that said these things agreed not together, in the place, nor in the day, nor in them that saw, as the writings they left behind bear witness unto this day.[^219]

[v]But Jesus was not dead; for God had said unto him, O Jesus! I will take thee and raise thee up unto Myself, and purify thee from those who disbelieve; and so it came to pass.[^217] [v]And God made the sayings that went around a trial for the people, and a source of hope for them that believed in him. [v]Thus doth God help and honour His messengers, and createth for His righteous servants a way when there appeareth to be no way.[^237] [v]For God is full of mercy and grace for men, but most of them are ever prone to reject faith, and they make their own gods besides Him.
### God’s Favour upon Jesus

[q5:110]And on Judgment Day God will say, “O Jesus, son of Mary! Remember My favour upon you and your mother: how I supported you with the holy spirit[^224] so you spoke to people in your infancy and adulthood. How I taught you writing, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel. How you healed the blind and the lepers—by My Will. How you brought the dead to life—by My Will. How I prevented the Children of Israel from harming you when you came to them with clear proofs and the disbelievers among them said, “This is nothing but pure magic.” [q5:111]And how I inspired the disciples, “Believe in Me and My messenger!” They declared, “We believe and bear witness that we fully submit to God.”[^225][^226]
### Jesus Denying Claim to Divinity

[q5:116]And on Judgment Day God will say, “O Jesus, son of Mary! Did you ever ask the people to worship you and your mother as gods besides God?” He will answer, “Glory be to You! How could I ever say what I had no right to say? If I had said such a thing, you would have certainly known it. You know what is hidden within me, but I do not know what is within You. Indeed, You alone are the Knower of all unseen. [q5:117]I never told them anything except what You ordered me to say: “Worship God—my Lord and your Lord!” And I was witness over them as long as I remained among them. But when You took me,[^227] You were the Witness over them—and You are a Witness over all things. [q5:118]If You punish them, they belong to You after all.[^228] But if You forgive them, You are surely the Almighty, All-Wise.” [q5:119]God will declare, “This is the Day when only the faithful will benefit from their faithfulness. Theirs are Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. That is the ultimate triumph.” [q5:120]To God alone belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything within. And He is Most Capable of everything.[^229]
## Closing
### The Qur’an Is a Confirmation

[q10:37]It is not possible for this Quran to have been produced by anyone other than God. In fact, it is a confirmation of what came before, and an explanation of the Scripture. It is, without a doubt, from the Lord of all worlds. Or do they claim, “He[^230] made it up!”? Tell them O Prophet, “Produce one chapter like it then, and seek help from whoever you can—other than God—if what you say is true!”[^231][^232]
### God’s Absolute Oneness
[q112:1]Say, O Prophet, “He is God, One and Indivisible; [q112:2]God—the Sustainer, needed by all.”[^233]
### One True God

[q2:255]God! There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who could possibly intercede with Him without His permission? He fully knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them, but no one can grasp any of His knowledge—except what He wills to reveal. His Seat encompasses the heavens and the earth, and the preservation of both does not tire Him. For He is the Most High, the Greatest.[^234]

[q59:22][q59:23]“He is God—there is no god worthy of worship except Him: Knower of the seen and unseen. He is the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful. He is God—there is no god except Him: the King, the Most Holy, the All-Perfect, the Source of Serenity, the Watcher of all, the Almighty, the Supreme in Might, the Majestic. notes.5:
A Gospel is the life story of Jesus told so as to bring out its significance for faith and history. It is necessarily revelatory and prophetic, since it assesses the significance of Jesus for the past and also for the future, and so differs from a historian’s “life of Jesus.” This narrative is written in the light of the revelation made to the prophet Muhammad. The Qur’an, the collection of revelatory messages received by Muhammad, contains ninety-three verses that refer to Jesus; with those on his mother, on John and on Zachariah, 145 verses bear on his story, and they are gathered in 45 passages on the page of Qur’anic passages. Directly or indirectly they speak of almost every aspect of his story: his family, birth and childhood, the nature of his person and his traditional titles, his miracles and message, the rejection by the Jews, his death and exaltation, and the significance of his work for Jewish history and for the history of the world. In this way the Qur’an gives a fairly complete outline of the life and work of Jesus.

That outline is supplemented here with background material drawn mostly from the New Testament, at times transformed in accordance with the Qur’anic revelation, to form a Gospel of approximately the size of Mark. Extensive notes explain, support and enlarge the picture of Jesus presented in the text, and give references to source passages, mainly from the Qur’an and the New Testament. The aim is to present the Qur’anic Jesus active in his own time and place and among his own people. The results and debates of modern critical research on the New Testament are kept in mind throughout.

A new Gospel is justified in our age. With twenty centuries of history and generations of critical research behind it, the present age is in a better position to assess the significance of the work of Jesus than were the ancient writers of the New Testament. The Gospels of the earliest centuries are indispensable for any such assessment, yet they do not themselves provide the best one. The fact that the four canonical Gospels contradict one another on almost every point, together with the growing recognition of this fact among Christians, calls for a second coming of Gospels and a rediscovery of Jesus. The schools of New Testament scholarship cannot supply a new Gospel. Their work is essentially negative: they can show the inadequacy of an existing Gospel but cannot offer one of their own. A Gospel is a revelatory work rather than a historical one and must spring from revelation, and the ninety-three Qur’anic verses about Jesus offer a revelatory basis for it.

On the Muslim view, the canonical Gospels are not reliable sources for the life and teachings of Jesus. They contain inconsistencies, contradictions, modifications and manipulations concerning his identity, birth, miracles, death and teachings, as anyone can see by setting any one story in a Gospel beside its parallel in another. Their authors are unknown, and none of them claims to be an eyewitness; the names Matthew, Mark, Luke and John were ascribed to the books later. The Gospels were written in Greek, not in the language of Jesus and his disciples, and decades after the events. No original copy exists, and the copies that survive were made centuries later and differ from one another in many places.

The Qur’an, according to the Muslim belief, is the direct word of God revealed to the prophet Muhammad through the angel Gabriel, and it has been preserved in its original language. It has been memorised in every generation since the revelation by millions of Muslims, and it was written down by the Companions who witnessed the revelation, some of whose manuscripts are still available. On this view the Qur’an supplies accurate information about the birth, miracles, teachings and relation to God of Jesus, and corrects the errors and inconsistencies found in the Gospels.

The words “verifying a word from God” can be understood in two ways:

a. “A word from God” may be understood as a promise of God, and “verifying” may be interpreted as “fulfilling.” Then the sense would be that John came in fulfillment of a promise of God, meaning that he was one of the figures whose coming was predicted in the Jewish prophetic tradition.

b. In Qur’an 3:45, Jesus is called “a word from God,” and so we may assume here a reference to Jesus and understand the verse as saying that John came confirming Jesus’ mission.

Both meanings are consistent with the Gospel tradition which presents John as a promised messianic figure (Mark 9:13; 1:6; Matt. 11:14; 17:12) as well as one who comes to prepare the way for Jesus (Luke 1:17, etc). Given the subtlety of the Qur’anic language, it seems likely that both meanings are intended.
notes.16: Qur’an 3:38-41; 19:7-15; Luke 1:9-25. The word “sammiyya” used in Qur’an 19.7 can mean “namesake,” but in the Qur’an, “name” is more than a word used to refer to a thing or a person: it is something that embodies the character of that thing (cf. Qur’an 2:31-33). Consequently, “sammiyya” means one sharing with a person or thing a name and the character described by that name. Now “John,” in Hebrew Yohanan, means “God favoured him,” and, therefore, the meaning of the Qur’anic verse would be that there was no one before John who was truly favored of God and was so named.
notes.17: Mark (1:6; 9:13) and Matthew (11:14; 17:12) identify John with Elias, who was believed to return in the last days (Mal. 4:5-6). The Gospel of John; however, expressly and firmly denies this identification (1:19-25). A possible synthesis of the two traditions is provided by Luke, which says that John came “in the spirit and power of Elias” (1:17). To these facts we must add the observation that in the Jewish tradition, especially the Qumran tradition, which is known to influence Christianity greatly, there existed expectation of three messianic figures: a priest of the house of Aaron, a king of the line of David, and a prophet of the category of Moses; moreover, Elias was sometimes believed to return as the (messianic) priest of the house of Aaron, who was to come in the company of the messianic king. (See G. R. Driver, The Judean Scrolls, Schocken Books, New York, 1965, pp. 464-466.) All this seems to suggest the view, taken in this narrative, that John and Jesus corresponded to the figures of the messianic priest and the messianic king, and that we should not take the identification of John the Baptist with Elias made by Mark and Matthew literally, but, like Luke, take it to mean that the Baptist performed the same role that Elias was sometimes believed to perform at his return, namely, the role of the messianic priest. This view is also consistent with the Qur’an, which accepts Jesus as the Messiah (see note 19) and while making a distinction between John and Elias (6:85) does suggest that the Baptist was one of the figures promised to Israel. (See note 15.)

What it does not do is fill it with the content of Jewish expectation: Jesus is the Messiah as a servant and messenger of God (4:172; 5:75), not as a king who restores the throne of David by arms. The gospels record that Jesus did not proclaim the title before the crowds and bade his disciples keep it (Mark 8:27-30), and this narrative keeps that reticence, because a messiahship declared openly would have been heard as a claim to kingship, which is the charge on which he was brought to Pilate (Luke 23:2). Qur’an 61:6. In Isaiah 9:6, one of the name’s of a promised figure is given in Hebrew as “Pele.” This name can be translated as “Admirable.” and indeed it is so translated in the Vulgate. The expectation of the figure of Isaiah 9:6 as well as the title ‘Admirable’ was current among the Qumran people (see Hymns III in G. Vermes’ translation, The Dead Sea Scrolls in English, Penguin Books, 1975), and there is some warrant for the view that the Qumran sectarians identified this figure, whom they also called Geber, Man, with the Messianic Prophet believed to be promised in Deuteronomy 18:18-19 (cf. G. Vermes, op. cit. p. 50). Since the Qumran tradition is known to have played a considerable part in the formation of Christianity, it is a plausible explanation of Qur’an 61.6 that the expection of the messianic prophet under the name Admirable was taken over by Christian tradition. Of course, as glorification of Jesus increased, Christianity lost inclination to expect an independent figure after Jesus and, in the main, began to see in Jesus the only bringer of salvation. Nevertheless, the New Testament has preserved evidence that shows that tradition sometimes expected not one but three messianic figures. Thus, in the Gospel of John (1:19-21, 25), the messengers sent from Jerusalem ask John the Baptist, “Who art thou?” and when he confessed, “I am not the Christ (i.e., the Messiah),” they asked him, “What then? Art thou Elias?” Again the Baptist denies, and this prompts the messengers’ next question, “Art thou that Prophet?” The Baptist denies even that, and then the messengers ask him, “Why baptizest thou then, if thou be not the Christ, nor Elias, neither that Prophet?”

In another passage of the same gospel, people argue among themselves about Jesus: “Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is that Prophet. Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, Shall Christ come out of Galilee?” (7:40-41).

The evidence for the expectation of three messianic figures is not limited to the fourth gospel. The same expectation is presupposed in the synoptic account of Jesus’ transfiguration (Mark 9:2-13; Matt. 17:1-13; Luke 9:28-36) in which Jesus the Messiah appears to his close disciples in the company of Elias and Moses (who was often believed to return in the role of “that Prophet”). The earliest tradition, of course, saw the Messiah in Jesus and Elias in John the Baptist, but does not present us with any person corresponding to the figure of Moses redivivus or that Prophet; we must therefore assume that this latter figure was expected to come soon after John and Jesus. This expectation of Moses or a figure like him, soon abandoned by the mainstream Christianity, seems to have survived in some Eastern Christian circles and given rise to hopes for a messenger bearing the title Admirable.

Following the story of the births of John and Jesus by the prophecies about the coming of Muhammad reflects the position, taken in this narrative, that the three prophets form the three figures that Israel awaited, with John corresponding to the messianic priest (or, Elias, or, in the language of the Qumran Scrolls, the messiah of Aaron), Jesus corresponding to the messianic king (or the Messiah of Israel), and Muhammad to the messianic prophet (or “that prophet” of John 1:20, 25; 7:40). To say that John, Jesus, and Muhammad correspond to the three messianic figures expected in the Jewish tradition cannot be true in the sense that they fulfill all what the tradition promised about those figures since the tradition is not consistent. One must go beyond the inconsistencies in detail and see what the Jewish messianism is really concerned with. And one must also rid it of some of its narrower, nationalistic concerns. If we do that, it would seem that the essential feature of the Jewish messianic thought, when it rises above nationalism and racialism, is the prediction that there will arise in the world up to three eschatological (or last) envoys from God who will usher in a final stage in human history during which there will be a period of dramatic improvement in man’s spiritual and material condition. And in view of the influence of John, Jesus, and Muhammad in history, it seems justified to regard them as the three promised eschatological messengers even though they do not fulfill some of the specific predictions found in the Jewish messianic tradition.

Luke 2:21-25, 28, 34. By a phenomenon rather frequent in the Gospels, this incident is duplicated in Luke 2:36-38, where it is an eighty-four years old woman, Anna, who acclaims the infant Jesus the future Saviour. Although none of the incidents is mentioned by any other gospel, they are not implausible since there must have been quite a few poor old people roaming among the temple visitors and heaping adulations on infants in the hope of flattering their parents into greater alms. However, what Luke puts in the mouth of Simeon and Anna reflects in large measure his own view of Jesus as a universal messenger. But as modern critical scholarship has shown, such a view was not shared by Jesus himself. For if he hesitated even to heal a non-Jewish girl (Mark 7:24-28) and did not want to throw bread (ie., teaching) to the Gentile dogs, and if he instructed the apostles to restrict their mission only to “the lost sheep of the house of Israel” (Matt. 10:5-6), it cannot be maintained that he presented himself as a light to lighten the Gentiles. Here the historical validity of the two Gospel reports cited is immaterial; for in any case they point to a serious conflict among Christians concerning the Gentile mission, and such a conflict could not have arisen if Jesus was as clear of his universal role as Simeon and Luke are.

The conclusion of critical scholarship that Jesus did not direct his teachings to the Gentile world is consistent with the Qur’an, which presents Jesus as “a messenger of God to Israel” (3:49, etc). However, the Qur’an does not lose sight of the fact that Jesus’ story came to be told among all the nations but takes it into account by saying that God made Mary and “her son a sign for all the nations” (21:91), a description that is also applicable to Noah’s story (29:15) and does not mean that Mary or Jesus or Noah was a universal Saviour in the sense the Gentile Christianity came to regard Jesus.

notes.56:
Mark 1:9-11; Matt. 3:13-17; Luke 3:21-23. The Gospels and the subsequent Christian tradition show great discomfort at the fact that Jesus went to John to be baptized by him and that it was this baptism that was in some way instrumental in opening the heavens to him. This discomfort is apparent as one follows tradition from the first Gospel to the fourth and beyond. Mark, and the other three Gospels, find it necessary to make John prophesy that there will come “one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose” (1:7). Matthew apparently thought that after such a prophecy, it is not fitting that John should baptize Jesus without saying something in recognition of his inferiority and so he modified Mark 1:9-10 by putting the following words in the Baptist’s mouth, “I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?” (Matt. 3:14). Luke so rewords the whole incident as to suggest that the opening of heavens to Jesus and the descent of the Holy Spirit in the shape of a dove might have taken place after the imprisonment of John (and not immediately after the baptism) and as a result of Jesus’ own practice of praying (3:19-22). The unknown author of the fourth Gospel, probably realizing the inadequacy of the other Evangelists’ solutions to the problem, omits all reference to the baptism and instead embarks on a systematic polemic against the Baptist (John 1:6-8, 15, 19-34; 3:22-36). The climax of all this reaches in the “Pseudo Clementines” where animosity against the Baptist completely overturns the original high regard for him in the heart of Jesus and his disciples as well as his usefulness as the forerunner of the Messiah and he is declared to be the Antichrist! (Hom. II, 17; cf. Recog. III, 61).

The Qur’an, which does not mention the baptism, presents both Jesus and John as great prophets without clearly suggesting the superiority of one over the other. It, indeed, does not seem to be profitable to concern ourselves with the question of who is superior to whom among the prophets, especially if the main object of our veneration is God and not His prophets, but in case of Jesus and John, the question is also not easy to settle. For, while Jesus was destined to have a tremendous influence on history, John was destined to be the prophet who influenced Jesus’ thinking and provided the platform for his work. Without John, there may not have been the Christ Jesus, and without Jesus, John’s mission may have died soon after his own death. In the Gospels, the stories of the births of Jesus and John, of their missions, and of their deaths are tied together in such a way that it is not possible to look at any one of them in isolation or to subordinate the work of one to the other.
